question: A 2-week-old infant is brought to the emergency room because of 4 episodes of bilious vomiting and inconsolable crying for the past 3 hours. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. An upper GI contrast series shows the duodenojejunal junction to the right of the vertebral midline; an air-filled cecum is noted in the right upper quadrant. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

options.opc: Arrested rotation of ventral pancreatic bud
options.opd: Hypertrophy and hyperplasia of the pyloric sphincter
options.ope: Resorption of a small bowel segment

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bilious vomiting and inconsolable crying" -> "intestinal obstruction" -> "abnormal positioning of duodenojejunal junction" -> "incomplete intestinal rotation" -> 80% CHAIN: "Abnormal positioning of duodenojejunal junction" -> "right of vertebral midline" -> "incomplete intestinal rotation" -> 75% CHAIN: "Air-filled cecum in right upper quadrant" -> "incomplete intestinal rotation" -> 80%
analysis: The presentation of bilious vomiting and abnormal positioning of the duodenojejunal junction and cecum on imaging suggest a malrotation of the intestines. Incomplete intestinal rotation is the most likely cause of this patient's condition.
